title: VPC observability playbook — terraform sketch & upgrade notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook sketch for setting up and upgrading observability in private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Focus areas: Prometheus + Grafana provisioning, OTEL collector patterns, and log shipping (Fluent Bit/Filebeat) using Terraform modules. This doc mixes design notes, terraform snippets, upgrade/runbook steps and outstanding questions.

Context and constraints (private envs):
- Often air-gapped or restricted egress; cannot assume external SaaS endpoints.
- Customer responsibility for long-term storage or we deploy customer-managed long-term store (remote_write receiver inside VPC).
- Cross-account VPC peering and strict security controls (SGs, NACLs).
- Terraform state sometimes stored in customer S3/GCS or our remote backend with restricted access.
- Need low blast radius: observability stack can be optional/sidecar to core services.

Goals for modules and playbook:
- Provide reusable terraform modules customers can fork: ri-obs-prometheus, ri-obs-grafana, ri-obs-otel, ri-obs-logs.
- Support both k8s (daemonsets/statefulsets) and VM systemd deployments.
- Upgrade path that preserves metrics history and minimizes alert noise.
- Secure defaults: mTLS, auth for Grafana, encrypted secrets (KMS/HSM), and network policies.

High-level architecture options (choose per-customer):
1) All-in-cluster: Prometheus statefulset + Grafana deployment + OTEL collector (daemonset) + Fluent Bit (ds).
   - Pros: simple networking, single deployment surface.
   - Cons: resource contention on shared clusters, harder to isolate.
2) Dedicated observability cluster in customer VPC: isolated cluster for observability workloads with reserved nodes/GPU not required.
   - Pros: predictable performance and easier upgrades.
   - Cons: extra cost and networking setup.
3) Hybrid: Prometheus node-exporters on app clusters remote_write to central Prometheus remote_write receiver or Cortex/Thanos cluster in observability cluster.
   - Recommended for larger customers.

Terraform module notes (sketches / interface suggestions):
- Module: ri-obs-prometheus
  - Inputs (vars): prometheus_version, storage_size_gb, retention_days, remote_write_endpoints (list), scrape_configs (string/file), enable_alertmanager (bool), alertmanager_config (map/string)
  - Outputs: prometheus_endpoint, prometheus_service_account, pvc_name
  - Notes: support both statefulset (k8s) and managed instance (systemd on VM using a generated systemd unit + config).

- Module: ri-obs-grafana
  - Inputs: grafana_version, admin_password_kms_key (or secret manager ref), provisioning_dashboards (list of local paths), ldap_config (optional), ingress_host, enable_basic_auth
  - Outputs: grafana_url, grafana_admin_user_secret
  - Notes: Provision dashboards via provisioning directory; recommend immutable provisioning to avoid drift during upgrades.

- Module: ri-obs-otel
  - Inputs: mode = [daemonset, sidecar, standalone-collector], otel_collector_version, receiver_bind_addresses, exporter_configs (map), instrumentations (list)
  - Outputs: otel_collector_service
  - Notes: Support two OS deployment patterns: k8s daemonset and systemd unit that embeds collector binary + config. For very restricted networks, include a local buffer file exporter to disk.

- Module: ri-obs-logs
  - Inputs: shipper_type = [fluentbit, filebeat], outputs (e.g., http/graylog/loki/s3), parsers (custom files), multiline_patterns
  - Outputs: log_forwarder_endpoint
  - Notes: Add file-based backpressure handling for transient endpoint outages; support compressed batches to save bandwidth.

Terraform versioning & provider notes:
- Lock terraform to 1.6.x for now in module templates.
- Pin k8s and helm provider versions in examples and use provider constraints in modules to avoid drift in different customer accounts.
- Add explicit migration guide for provider major upgrades; recommend running `terraform plan` in a staging workspace before prod.
- State handling: provide examples for using remote backend in customer account (S3 with encryption + DDB locking) or in our managed backend with tightly scoped IAM roles.

Example prometheus remote_write snippet (for customers that want central long-term store):
- remote_write:
  - url: https://central-remote-recv.internal.cluster:9201/api/v1/push
    basic_auth:
      username: "ri-write"
      password_file: "/etc/prom/remote_write_pass"
    queue_config:
      capacity: 2500
      max_shards: 10
      min_shards: 1

OTEL collector patterns and config hints:
- For k8s: prefer daemonset with a small memory buffer (2-4Gi) and a robust retry/wiretap exporter to avoid data loss during outages.
- For VMs: provide an install script that drops /etc/otel-collector/config.yaml and creates a systemd unit `otel-collector.service` managed by the module.
- Example exporter config: use OTLP over HTTP with mTLS to the downstream receiver.

Log shipping recommendations:
- Use Fluent Bit for lightweight edge forwarding; Filebeat when heavy parsing required.
- Run a local aggregator in the observability cluster (Loki or Vector) to accept forwarded logs and provide retention.
- For audit logs or PCI-sensitive logs, avoid third-party endpoints — send to customer-managed S3 or internal ELK.

Security and secrets:
- Grafana admin password: provision via KMS-encrypted secret. Avoid hard-coded static admin passwords in templates.
- TLS: use cert-manager (k8s) backed by customer private CA, or accept certs via Terraform input.
- mTLS between OTEL forwards and receivers; recommend SPIFFE/SPIRE for identity when available.

Upgrade plan (prometheus/grafana/otel) — sketch of playbook steps:
1) Preflight (one week before change):
   - run `promtool check-config` on candidate configs.
   - export current rule groups and dashboard jsons to backup bucket.
   - ensure alertmanager silences or maintenance windows ready.
   - smoke test remote_write receiver connectivity (from staging).
2) Stage canary:
   - deploy new module version to a single canary namespace/cluster or a single replicate pod in k8s.
   - metrics to watch: scrape success rate, series churn, CPU/memory, remote_write queue length.
   - if Prometheus TSDB format changes, run conversion in canary only.
3) Gradual rollout (24–72h):
   - ramp up nodes/instances across remaining clusters, monitor for increased compaction or memory spikes.
   - watch for alert surge; automatically mute expected alerts via automation.
4) Full rollout and cleanup:
   - finalize terraform apply for all modules.
   - remove canary silences and re-enable alerts.
   - rotate Grafana admin tokens if part of upgrade.
5) Rollback plan:
   - keep previous docker images and helm charts available for quick redeploy.
   - terraform: use `terraform state mv` and `terraform apply` with previous module version in a recovery workspace.
   - if TSDB upgrade fails, restore from snapshot (explicitly keep recent snapshots for 72h).

Runbook checklist (quick ops steps):
- Pre-upgrade: backups taken (TSDB snapshot), grafana db dumped, alertmanager config backed up.
- During upgrade: set notification to on-call, create ephemeral channel, enable detailed logs.
- Post-upgrade: run smoke dashboards, verify scrape targets = expected, check remote_write success rate > 99%.

Testing and automation suggestions:
- Create a CI pipeline that applies module changes to a disposable k8s cluster and runs a validation script (scrapes up, dashboards present, can write/read remote_write).
- Include chaos tests: kill collector pods, saturate network to simulate egress loss and confirm buffers behave correctly.

Operational tips and gotchas observed in pilots:
- Prometheus memory usage spikes when scrape targets increase cardinality; tune scrape_interval and relabeling rules early.
- Grafana provisioning can drift if users manually edit dashboards; use provisioning files and disable save-by-users in strict modes.
- OTEL exporter retries can cause OOM if buffers are unbounded; set bounded queue_config.
- Terraform provider upgrades sometimes force resource recreation (helm provider in particular). Pin versions in module root and document upgrade steps.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default long-term store: Thanos vs Cortex vs Loki (for logs) per-customer recommendation table.
- Should we provide an option for embedded Cortex receive endpoints in module, or always recommend a separate infra module?
- Standardize label conventions for tenant and service to avoid cardinality blowups.
- Create a migration tool for Prometheus TSDB format upgrades to run offline.

Next steps (for this draft):
- Lina to prototype ri-obs-otel module with systemd example (due 2026-03-12).
- Owen to produce a Terraform example repo that demonstrates modular composition (ri-obs-prometheus + ri-obs-grafana) using a customer S3 backend.
- Diego to run a canary upgrade test in staging and post metrics snapshot to the linked Confluence page.

Quick references (internal):
- Confluence: OBS-PRIVATE-VPC-PLAYBOOK (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub module examples: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/tree/main/observability
- Jira epic: PD-4800 (observability infra for private deployments)

Notes to self: keep playbook minimal and prescriptive. Customers will want flexible knobs, but defaults should be safe for small teams (single-cluster) and discoverable for enterprise (dedicated cluster).

-- end of draft --
